name: sol_ec_7
description: External call without gas limit enabling gas-exhaustion denial-of-service
question: The source file in `source` contains a function that performs an external call (e.g., to a fee receiver, order counterparty, or callback/hook) using call() or similarly low-level call without specifying a gas limit or fixed gas stipend, and has critical follow-up logic (state updates, payouts to other parties, or continued loop execution) that executes after that call, such that a malicious or malfunctioning callee can consume all forwarded gas to prevent that follow-up logic from completing, causing a denial of service; this excludes calls restricted to trusted/immutable admin addresses, calls wrapped with an explicit fixed gas limit or try/catch gas cap, and calls with no dependent logic afterward.
criteria: A function loops over multiple external addresses (e.g., fee receivers) calling each with call() without a per-call gas limit, so one malicious receiver can consume all gas and block payment to the remaining recipients

An external call forwards all remaining gas to an untrusted callback or order-fill target with no gas stipend or gas cap specified, and subsequent state-finalizing code depends on that call returning promptly

A function executes an external call to an arbitrary or user-supplied address using call{value: ...}() without any gas argument, followed by required bookkeeping (e.g., marking an order filled or updating balances) that never runs if the callee consumes all gas

A batch-processing function calls out to each item's handler via low-level call without limiting the gas passed, allowing a single poisoned item to exhaust gas and halt processing of the rest of the batch
